title: Air-fryer chicken tikka
subtitle: Yoghurt-marinated chicken in the air fryer for tandoor-like charring.
excerpt: Boneless chicken thighs marinated in yoghurt, spices, and lemon juice, then air-fried at high heat for the charred edges and smoky flavour of restaurant tikka without a clay oven. Serves four.
sourceNotes: Chicken tikka is a dish from the Indian subcontinent, traditionally cooked in a tandoor oven at very high heat. The yoghurt marinade tenderises the meat and carries the spice coating. The air fryer replicates the high convection heat of the tandoor at a domestic scale.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the marinated raw chicken for up to 3 months. Thaw overnight in the fridge and cook from cold.
recipe.batchNotes: Double the marinade and batch. Cook in two rounds if the basket won't fit all pieces in a single layer.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Marinate for up to 24 hours in the fridge for deeper flavour.

content.text: Chicken tikka needs a hot, dry environment to char properly. The air fryer at 220°C delivers this: the circulating heat dries the yoghurt coating fast, giving the lightly charred edges that define good tikka. Boneless thighs work better than breast here because they stay moist at high heat.
Marinate for at least 2 hours, longer if you have time. The yoghurt tenderises the meat and the spices penetrate further with more time in the fridge.

items.prepNote: cut into large chunks, about 4 cm

content.text: Combine {{plain-yoghurt}} of yoghurt, {{lemon-juice}} of lemon juice, {{garlic}} of grated garlic, and {{ginger-root}} of grated ginger in a large bowl. Add {{garam-masala}} of garam masala, {{cumin-ground}} of cumin, {{turmeric}} of turmeric, {{paprika-smoked}} of smoked paprika, {{chilli-powder}} of chilli powder, and {{sea-salt-fine}} of salt. Stir well. Add the {{chicken-thighs-boneless}} chunks and toss until coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours.

Preheat the air fryer to 220°C. Shake excess marinade from the chicken pieces and place in a single layer in the basket. Spray lightly with cooking oil. Cook for 9 minutes, turn the pieces, and cook for a further 7-9 minutes until charred at the edges and cooked through. Serve with flatbreads, sliced red onion, and mint yoghurt.

items.cause: Too much marinade left on, or temperature too low.
items.fix: Shake off excess marinade before cooking. Make sure the fryer is fully preheated to 220°C.

items.cause: Breast used instead of thigh, or overcooked.
items.fix: Use boneless thighs. They stay moist at high heat where breast meat dries out quickly.

items.cause: Yoghurt dripping into the fryer pan.
items.fix: Empty and wipe the drip tray halfway through. A small amount of smoking is normal at 220°C.

items.cause: Marinated for less than an hour.
items.fix: The minimum is 2 hours; 8-24 hours is noticeably better. Plan ahead.

content.text: Chicken tikka in the air fryer takes about 20 minutes of active work plus marinating time. Good as part of a spread with rice, dhal, and pickles, or served in wraps with shredded lettuce and mint yoghurt.
